d: First Speaker Odile Ferrant of the Meridian Compact: a poised broadcast-priestess in her fifties, indigo sash-collared suit with a silver concentric wave-ring pectoral, greying chignon, a microphone-gavel in one hand, the calm authority of the airwaves

Marshal-Director Anton Bragg of the Vosk Union: a broad bunker-born marshal in a rust-orange greatcoat and slate wedge cap, chest heavy with medal wedges, jaw like a blast door, grey stubble and tireless suspicious eyes

Voivode Irina Volkonskaya of Novaya Zaslon: a fallout aristocrat in a bone-white fur mantle, a pale radiation scar across her cheek that her court calls the light, antique revolver at her hip, proud fatalistic gaze

Caliph-Mechanic Yusuf al-Arrani of the Chrome Caliphate: a brass-robed artificer-priest, green turban wound with copper filament, burnished gauntlets, wise narrow face and oiled beard, hands that know every machine in the Brassworks

Refectrix Tomoe Ishikawa of the Showa Refectory: an immaculate ruler in red-and-white work-formal dress, steel chrysanthemum comb in dark hair, white work-gloves, the serene exact gaze of the eternal shift
Doge Remo Vellano of the Free Ports of Cascara: a smuggler-lord in a teal frock coat with a gold lantern pin, weathered sailor face under grey curls, chart tattoos at the cuffs, a bargaining smile

President-Caudillo Bruno Salgado of the Grande Territorio: a rail empire grandee in yellow-and-green parade sash, magnificent cavalry moustache, locomotive-spur boots, expansive roguish grin under a braided peaked cap
Dominus Kaeth Varo of the Antakan Dominion: a pale vault-priest in an ash-grey cassock, an iron door-ring stole, keys of office at the belt, cold serene authority and unblinking conviction

Wardens-Kol Bree Andhal of the Rustwalkers: a nomad warden in layered scrap-leathers, antenna-totem staff in hand, windburned braided hair, scrapline scars on her forearms, the sharp easy smile of the open road
Speaker Anouk Bellamy of the Verdant League: a commune orator in homespun green with a wheat-antenna brooch, reading spectacles, a broadcast-listening earpiece, warm stubborn farm-belt face

Governor-General Marcus Bright of New Halcyon: a silver-tongued fixer in a flawless cerulean suit with a white peacock pin, silver cravat stick, immaculate manicured hands, a smile like a closing contract

Overseer Kesh Tamm of the Glasswake Combine: a salvage boss in a hazard-striped tanker jacket, green-glass dosimeter pendant on a cord, shaven-headed, weathered squint of the glasslands and a ledger-keeper’s frown

Voice-in-the-Snow Eirik Voss of the Frozen Signal: an ice-cult orator in a white parka with pale sine-wave trim, frost-reddened beard, headphones resting at his throat, the patient thousand-mile stare of a man who listens to static
General Kleber as his portraits show him: the giant of the egyptian expedition, a huge blond alsatian with the uniform of the cairo assassination
General Kleber as his portraits show him: the giant of the egyptian expedition, a huge blond alsatian with the uniform of the cairo assassination

Illyrio Mopatis as A Song of Ice and Fire imagines him: an enormously fat magister of Pentos, heavy-lidded amber eyes above a braided yellow beard, rings on every finger, silk robes over the girth of three men, soft-spoken and dangerous

Lord Walder Frey as A Song of Ice and Fire describes him: a wizened spindly man past ninety, sunken-cheeked with a spotted bald scalp and a thin white lip-hair, lean hard hands and watery eyes that miss nothing, mean and eternal

Maege Mormont, the She-Bear of Bear Island as the books imagine her: a stout weathered warrior-woman in mail and boiled leather, grey-streaked hair braided back, no interest in gowns, an axe at her hip like any of her daughters
Greatjon Umber as the books describe him: a huge boisterous northman, the largest man in the hall, shaggy-bearded, roaring laughter one moment and tearing a man's ear off with his bare hands the next
Rickard Stark of Karhold as A Song of Ice and Fire imagines him: a gaunt stern lord with a long grey beard and hard cold eyes, mail under a wool cloak, the face of a man counting grievances

Cregan Stark, the Old Man of the North as history remembers him: a hard young king of Winterfell in his prime, long brown hair, a stern bearded face beneath a bronze-and-iron crown, the man who ruled the hour after the Dance
Torrhen Stark, the King Who Knelt as the histories name him: a grim bearded king in furs and iron with a long sword at his hip, bending the knee at the Trident to save his people from dragonfire
Theon Stark, the Hungry Wolf as the old kings' names run: a lean ferocious king of Winterfell, long dark hair and beard, sea-raider scars across his face, mail and wolf-pelts, cruel and restless
Edmure Tully as A Song of Ice and Fire shows him: a young genial lord of Riverrun with the Tully auburn hair and a soft earnest face, good-hearted, gallant and a little too fond of his own generosity
Ser Brynden Tully, the Blackfish: a lean weathered knight past sixty, grey-streaked hair and beard, hardened soldier's face, black mail and black cloak, stubborn as the river itself

Queen Nymeria of the Rhoynar as Dorne remembers her: a burned-city queen with the bronze skin of the Rhoynar, dark hair braided long, a fire in her eyes, leading ten thousand ships across the sea to marry a Martell
Qhored Hoare, the Old Kraken as the ironborn remember him: a broad grey-bearded reaver-king, salt-stained braids, a great axe and mail shirts taken from drowned kings, cruel and canny

Argilac Durrandon, the Arrogant as history calls him: a tall storm-king with black hair and deep storm-blue eyes, a great black beard, crowned with antlers of hammered bronze, proud and reckless to the end

Sharra Arryn, the Falcon Queen of the Vale as the conquest era remembers her: a renowned beauty with dark hair and cool grey eyes, a silver moon-and-falcon circlet, regent mother of the boy king, offering herself to a dragonlord to save her realm

Lady Jeyne Arryn, the Maiden of the Vale as the Dance of Dragons remembers her: a sharp-featured proud noblewoman in sky-blue and silver, dark hair bound up beneath a moon-and-falcon brooch, gay and shrewd, a queen in all but name
Jeor Mormont, the Old Bear of the Night's Watch as the books describe him: a gruff bald old soldier with a great grey beard, a raven on his shoulder, black wool and roughspun, hard and kind at once

Qhorin Halfhand as the books describe him: a lean legendary ranger of the Watch, long grey hair, a face seamed by wind, two fingers lost to a wildling axe, sword and longknife in the other hand, quiet and deadly

Tormund Giantsbane as the books describe him: a broad jovial wildling giant with a thick white beard bound in gold rings, a booming laugh, layered shaggy furs, the soul of the free folk under all his tall tales

Xaro Xhoan Daxos as the books describe him: a wealthy Qartheen merchant-prince, smooth-shaven and bejeweled, a long pointed nose, silk and gemstones and a heavy jeweled nose-ring, smiling and bottomless

Aenar Targaryen, the Exile as Valyria's end remembers him: a pale silver-haired dragonlord in embroidered robes of deep red and black, lilac eyes, the man who sold everything and led his family west before the Doom

The young man who claims to be Aegon, Sixth of His Name: a silver-haired youth raised in exile, lilac Targaryen eyes, tall and lean, plain travel wool hiding the blood of the dragon, hopeful and rehearsed

Hizdahr zo Loraq as the books describe him: a Meereenese noble with a lean fussy frame, oiled vermillion hair in a pointed beard and elaborate hairstyles, gauzy tokars of cloth-of-gold, patient and ambitious
Kraznys mo Nakloz as the books describe him: a plump imperious Good Master of Astapor, perfumed and painted, a lacquered vermillion beard, gemmed nails and silk tokars, cruel behind his smile

Prince Jalabhar Xho as the books describe him: an exile prince of the Summer Isles, tall and ebony-skinned in a cloak of green-and-gold feathers, a tall red-feathered crest, gracious and perpetual at court

Círdan the Shipwright as Tolkien's canon describes him: an ancient Elven lord of the Grey Havens, oldest elf in Middle-earth, long silver beard reaching his girdle, keen grey eyes, simple grey robes, patient as the sea

Gil-galad, the last High King of the Noldor as the lays remember him: a tall stern Elven king with long dark hair, grey eyes like starlight, a silver helm crowned with a star and a spear of silver steel, the light of the elder days
Celeborn the Wise as Tolkien describes him: a tall lord of the Galadhrim, silver-haired and grave, grey-clad beneath a silver circlet, the calm counterweight to his wife's radiance

Amroth, king of Lórien as the old lays remember him: a fair Elven lord in silver-grey and mail, gold-laced hair beneath a slender circlet, restless with love, the last king before the Nimrodel ran dry
Oropher, king of the Woodland Realm as history remembers him: a proud Sindarin lord of Mirkwood, silver-gold hair beneath a crown of autumn berries and red leaves, wary of Noldor and dwarves alike

Treebeard as Tolkien describes him: the oldest Ent of Fangorn, fourteen feet tall, a bark-skinned figure with great root-like toes and twiggy grey hair, deep green-and-grey eyes under bushy brows, slow, deep-voiced and patient

Beorn the Skin-changer as The Hobbit describes him: a huge thick-armed man with black hair and a great beard, thick legs and shoulders, a broad honest face that goes from jolly to thunderous, dressed in wool and skins

Durin the Deathless as the dwarves' memory holds him: the first father of the Longbeards, a broad stately dwarf-lord with a braided iron-grey beard to his girdle, a crown-shaped mithril helm, the Deathless in the stone

Ar-Pharazôn the Golden as Tolkien describes him: a tall proud Númenórean king in his prime, golden-haired and golden-armored, a sceptre in one hand and a fleet behind him, the proudest man who ever lived
Tar-Palantir, the Seeing King of Númenor: a gaunt ascetic Númenórean king with deep-set eyes and silver-streaked dark hair, plain robes, mourning the broken line of kings and looking ever westward
King Eärnil II of Gondor as the annals remember him: a seasoned soldier-king with greying hair and a hard-won crown, a merciful victor's face, the last strong king before the waning
Arvedui, the Last King of Arthedain as the histories name him: a desperate northman king in a threadbare cloak, pale and unshaven, the red star of the North on his breast, fleeing the fall of Fornost
Araphant of Arthedain as the annals remember him: a grey-bearded king of the fading North, weary eyes beneath a thin silver circlet, rebuilding alliances no one else believes in
Amlaith of Fornost, first king of Arthedain: a stern northman lord dividing a broken realm, dark hair bound with a silver fillet, the pale star of the North on his shield
Amlaith of Fornost, first king of Arthedain: a stern northman lord dividing a broken realm, dark hair bound with a silver fillet, the pale star of the North on his shield
Malvegil of Arthedain as the annals remember him: a watchful king of the shrinking North, grey-cloaked beneath the star, reigning while Angmar's shadow first rose

Fréaláf Hildeson, first king of the Second Line of Rohan as the tales tell: a young horselord who slew Wulf in his hall at the end of the Long Winter, flaxen hair, byrnie and shield, crowned at Edoras by the hand of Saruman

Fréaláf Hildeson, first king of the Second Line of Rohan: a young horselord who slew Wulf in his hall at the end of the Long Winter, flaxen hair, byrnie and shield, crowned at Edoras by the hand of Saruman

Valandil, first king of Arnor as the annals remember him: a boy-king grown grave too early, Isildur's youngest son, dark-haired and pale beneath the silver crown of the North, ruling from Annúminas in a realm already failing

Brand of Dale as the end of the Third Age knows him: a bowman-lord descended from kings, broad and bearded in the manner of Dale, a great yew bow over his shoulder, standing before the gate as the East came down
Girion, Lord of Dale as the old songs remember him: a merchant-king of the lake-men, richly robed with a golden torque, the man whose arrows could not save Dale from the fire of the Dragon
Sangahyando of Umbar as the histories name him: a swarthy corsair-lord of Harad's blood, black-bearded and gold-ringed, a curved sword and a stolen banner, the terror of the coasts
Bolg of the North as The Hobbit names him: a huge goblin-armored chieftain, scarred hideous grey skin under riveted iron plates, a scimitar of savage make, crushing and vengeful

King Dongcheon of Goguryeo as Korean tradition holds him: a Korean warrior-king in iron lamellar and a gold diadem, the defend-all-his-life monarch who sheltered refugees and died fleeing the Wei legions
Queen Himiko of Yamatai as the Wei chronicles record her: a shaman-queen of ancient Japan, unmarried and unreadable, bronze mirrors at her shrine, robes of plain woven silk and a calm absolute gaze
Gongsun Kang of Liaodong as the chronicles remember him: a frontier warlord of the northeast, harsh and pragmatic, sending a warlord's head east in a box to buy peace with the Middle Kingdom
Tao Qian of Xu Province as the chronicles remember him: an aged kindly governor in Han robes and a worn cap, white-bearded, a man who wanted only to hand his poor province to someone worthier

Ma Chao of Xiliang as Romance of the Three Kingdoms paints him: a dashing young warlord of the western frontier, lion-helmeted and silver-armored, a long spear, called the Splendid for his looks and terrible in cavalry war
Zhang Bao of the Yellow Turbans as the tales tell him: a rebel general in hemp-yellow robes and a yellow turban, claiming wizardry in his father's Way of Great Peace, wild-eyed and doomed
Liu Yan of Yi Province as the chronicles remember him: an ambitious imperial clansman turned southwestern potentate, in minister's robes with a private emperor's air, scheming a dynasty in Sichuan
Li Jue as the chronicles remember him: a coarse Liang-general who seized Chang'an after his master's fall, scarred, armored in captured splendor, brutal and doomed
Chen Gong as the Romance paints him: a lean clever strategist with a thin beard and tireless anxious eyes, plain scholar's robes, serving hopeless lords with brilliant stubborn plans
Liu Cong as the chronicles remember him: a soft young lord of Jing who surrendered a province to spare himself, silken robes and a downcast face, his father's realm traded for a hollow title
Liu Qi as the tales remember him: the anxious elder son of Jing, drifting in fear of his stepmother's house, finding his footing only at the river with a borrowed fleet
Yuan Tan as the chronicles remember him: the eldest of the Yuan sons, a bitter armored heir fighting his own brother while the family's great name collapses, brave and graceless
Vizimir II of Redania as the books remember him: a red-bearded fat king grown thoughtful with age, silver and crimson, the merchant-friendly monarch murdered in the streets of his own capital

King Tankred Thyssen of Kovir as the books imagine him: a young restless crown of the rich northern kingdom, elegantly cut doublets and an inquisitive tilt of the head, rich beyond the wars to the south
King Demavend III of Aedirn as the books describe him: an indecisive arrogant king in laced crimson doublets, thinning hair and a sharp beard, assassinated on a barge and little mourned
Prince Stennis of Aedirn as the games paint him: a young doubting heir in blue and silver, clean-shaven with wavy hair, caught between father and people, all caution and no resolve

Eithné, queen of Brokilon as the books describe her: an ancient dryad queen in bark-brown living armor, a silver birch circlet, red-gold hair like autumn leaves, a bow older than any treaty, cold and eternal
Brouver Hoog as the books describe him: the ancient dwarven leader of Mahakam, a great grey forked beard to his belt, a massive torso in miner's leathers, shrewd eyes beneath brows like thatch

Hierarch Cyrus Hemmelfart as the games name him: the high priest of Novigrad's Eternal Fire, a heavy unctuous prelate in gilded red vestments, rings and a shaved tonsure, fire in his sermons and ledgers both
The Bloody Baron as the games paint him: a heavyset self-exiled Temerian officer, red stubbled face and drink-flushed cheeks, a soldier's coat gone shabby, blustering, brutal and broken-hearted

King Bran of the Skellige Isles as the games paint him: a grey-maned old sea-king with a braided beard wound with rings, fur cloak and a boar-spear, a ruler who crossed the sea to be buried on the tides
Coram II of Cintra as the books remember him: a stubborn old king of the Lion line, grey-bearded and iron-crowned, the grandfather who held the north border against Kaedwen
Fergus var Emreis as the books remember him: the last rightful emperor of Nilfgaard before the Usurper, a gentle scholar-sovereign in white and gold, destroyed with his son beside him
King Easar Togita of Shienar as the books describe him: a grey-templed Borderlander king in a topknot and lacquered armor strips over silk, weathered face, calm courtesy over a core of steel
King Paitar Nachiman of Arafel as the books describe him: a stocky Borderlander king with bells in his braided hair and forked blue-painted brows, courteous and quick as a drawn sword

Queen Ethenielle Kirukon Cosaru of Kandor as the books describe her: a grey-haired Borderlander queen in silk embroidered with gems, a small woman with a first-councillor's eye and a Borderlander's spine
Queen Tenobia of Saldaea as the books describe her: a young fierce queen with tilted dark eyes and a proud nose, a high-necked red dress and an iron betrothal necklace, wild as the Saldaean wind
Davram Bashere as the books describe him: a short compact Saldaean marshal with a gray-streaked pointed beard and dark tilted eyes, slim sword and knife, light on his feet and dangerous as a wolf
High Lord Darlin Sisnera of Tear as the books describe him: a broad tall Tairen lord with dark curly hair and a pointed beard, slashed velvet coats and rings, a great duelist grown into a general
King Alsalam of Arad Doman as the books describe him: a Domani king in elegant silk coats, silver-touched dark hair, the merchant court's silver tongue - and a monarch gone missing in his own wars
King Roedran of Murandy as the books describe him: a hawk-nosed southron king in wine-dark coats, pretending weakness while quietly building the only real army Murandy has ever had

Queen Alliandre Maritha Moghefah of Ghealdan as the books describe her: a handsome woman with black hair and sharp dark eyes, blue silk slashed with gold, brave enough to swear to the Dragon and mean it

Queen Tylin Quintara Mitsobar of Altara as the books describe her: a black-haired Ebou Dar queen with an hourglass figure and a beauty mark, green-and-red silks, a curved dagger at her belt and a bird of prey's smile
Mazrim Taim as the books describe him: a tall hard-faced channeler with dark curling hair and a hooked nose, black coat with dragon pins, powerful, controlled and unreadable
Prophet Masema Dagar as the books describe him: a gaunt wild-eyed zealot with lank dark hair, worn coats gone ragged, preaching the Dragon with a voice that burns crowds like kindling
Berelain sur Paendrag, First of Mayene as the books describe her: a raven-haired beauty in pale silks that suggest rather than hide, jewel-dark eyes, gracious, calculating and impossible to unseat

Nesta din Reas Two Moons, Mistress of the Ships of the Sea Folk as the books describe her: a weathered Windfinder-queen with gold rings piercing nose and ears, bare-footed silks, authority older than any shore throne

Elaida a'Roihan as the books describe her: the Amyrlin Seat of the White Tower, handsome and severe, dark hair in a bun beneath a striped stole, red-gold hair-serpent ring, absolutely certain and absolutely wrong

Lord Captain Commander Valda of the Children of the Light as the books describe him: a hard-bitten whitecloak officer, grey at the temples, polished armor and a white cloak with a golden sun, certainty as sharp as his sword
King Ailron of Amadicia as the books describe him: a weak king in a strong throne's shadow, silk coats and a nervous hand at his sword hilt, ruling the realm the Children actually run

High Lady Suroth of the Seanchan as the books describe her: a pale shaven-headed Seanchan noble with long lacquered fingernail sheaths, high-collared silks, the imperious patience of an empire's blood

Sevanna of the Shaido Aiel as the books describe her: a tall beautiful Aiel woman with red-gold hair and green eyes, ivory-and-gold bracelets, jealous, vain and utterly certain she deserves everything
Couladin of the Shaido as the books describe him: a raw-boned Aiel warrior with yellow-red hair and hard eyes, veiled and spear-armed, a false Car'a'carn's fire in his certainty
King Ramsis Dendup of Onderon as the shows paint him: an old mild exiled monarch in faded royal robes, weary honest eyes, a peaceful king in a war that will not let him be

Prime Minister Lama Su of Kamino as the films show him: a tall slender grey-skinned Kaminoan with a long neck and pale alien eyes, white robes and silver chains, a pleasant corporate voice over a cloning empire
Chairman San Hill of the InterGalactic Banking Clan as the shows paint him: a gaunt Muun financier, pale elongated head, immaculate dark robes, financing both sides with the same thin smile
Chairman Tion Medon of Utapau as the films show him: a tall pale Pau'an administrator with black-rimmed eyes and a lined elongated face, dark layered robes, greeting conquerors with dignified dread
Foreman Wat Tambor of the Techno Union as the shows paint him: an armored Skakoan in a metal pressure suit with a mechanical voice and goggles, greedy and precise, an engineer of war
Cham Syndulla of Ryloth as the shows paint him: a weathered Twi'lek freedom fighter with orange skin and heavy lekku, patched blaster-gear, the unbreakable will of a whole occupied world
Mother Talzin of the Nightsisters as the shows paint her: a pale green Dathomiri witch with silver-white hair in braids, bone-and-talisman robes, green magicks in her hands and vengeance in her eyes
Lando Calrissian as the films show him: a smooth charming gambler-administrator in a blue-and-gold cape over a light shirt, a neat moustache and easy grin, trustworthy precisely when it counts
Breha Organa of Alderaan as the shows paint her: a stately dark-haired queen with soft-lined patient eyes, white ceremonial gowns and the regality of a dying peaceful world
Queen Jamillia of Naboo as the films show her: a young monarch in the crimson-and-gold throne gown of Naboo, the white makeup and red scar of remembrance, wise beyond her few years

Admiral Ar'alani of the Chiss Ascendancy as the books describe her: a coldly composed Chiss flag officer with glowing red eyes, blue-black hair, white uniform with rank patches, precise and unimpeachable in command
First Minister Shakaar Edon of Bajor as the shows paint him: a weathered former resistance fighter turned statesman, thick dark hair, rugged Bajoran earring, a farmer's hands and a rebel's patience
Kai Winn Adami of Bajor as the shows paint her: a severe woman in elaborate crimson-and-teal Kai's vestments, ornate headdress, half-lidded eyes and honeyed venom, devout and grasping at once
Ambassador Sarek of Vulcan as the shows paint him: a stately elderly Vulcan with silver hair swept back, sharp cheekbones, dark robes of state, absolute logic behind old sorrow

T'Pau of Vulcan as the shows paint her: an austere elderly matriarch with silver braided hair, ornate Vulcan robes and ceremonial jewelry, unbending dignity, the only one who ever refused a seat on the Federation Council

Commander Thy'lek Shran of the Andorian Imperial Guard as the shows paint him: a blue-skinned Andorian with white hair, antennae twitching at every mood, silver Imperial Guard uniform and an aggressive honor all his own

Archduke Armand Ecaz of the Ecazi court as the books imagine him: a proud noble of the League in gauzy ceremonial robes, a sculpted silver beard, jealous of Harkonnen slights and protective of his daughter's hand

Count Ilban Richese of House Richese as the books imagine him: a compact industrious noble of a tech-saturated world, brocade robes over a merchant's build, perpetually outmaneuvered by Ix and furious about it

Siridar-Duke Hundro Moritani of Grumman as the books imagine him: a vengeful warlike noble in black-and-red armor-trim, scarred knuckles, a thin moustache and a duel-hungry grin, his whole house a running grudge

Dominic Vernius, the renegade Earl of Ix as the books imagine him: a stocky brilliant engineer-king in exile, grey-shot hair, worn workman's clothes over a noble spine, dynamite in his heart and grief behind his eyes
Prince Rhombur Vernius of Ix as the books imagine him: a bluff hearty noble turned cyborg after Tleilaxu treachery, half his face restored metal, loyalty like a hammer, hope like a wound
Scytale of the Tleilaxu as the books imagine him: a sleek last-master shapeshifter in gray-silver robes, bland forgettable features that are a lie, the face of the Bene Tleilax turned sly and eternal
Reverend Mother Gaius Helen Mohiam as the books and films imagine her: an ancient Bene Gesserit in voluminous black aba robes, a chain of rank, a reed of a body and eyes that see through you entire

Liet-Kynes, the Imperial Planetologist and Fremen judge-of-the-change as the books imagine him: a sun-browned desert man in stillsuit and Fremen wraps, beard and hair covered by a hood, blue-in-blue eyes that measure only water and truth
Chani of the Fremen as the books and films imagine her: a young desert warrior-woman with blue-in-blue eyes, dark hair bound beneath a stillsuit hood, a crysknife at her belt, fierce and devoted

Lieutenant Commander Kurt Ambrose, SPARTAN-051 as the books describe him: a broad Spartan officer with bleached-blond hair and wolfish patience, ONI black fatigues, the trainer who made the Spartan-IIIs and died buying them time
Thel 'Vadam, the Arbiter as the games show him: a Sangheili warrior-lord in silver-blue combat harness, four-jawed head held high, energy sword at hand, honor reclaimed through heresy and war

Fleet Admiral Lord Terrence Hood as the games show him: a composed UNSC commander with grey hair and a service dress uniform heavy with ribbons, orbital fleet command in his bearing and Earth's defense in his voice

Sergeant Major Avery Johnson as the games show him: a veteran Marine with a shaved head, deep voice and cigar, battle armor scorched from a hundred deployments, swearing like scripture and dying like a legend

Captain Jacob Keyes of the UNSC Pillar of Autumn as the games show him: a lean greying naval officer in UNSC dress greys, calm eyes over a mind for the Keyes Loop, pipe tobacco and impossible maneuvers
Serin Osman of ONI as the books show her: a composed ex-Spartan admiral with dark hair pinned back, naval uniform and a prosthetic hand under the glove, Warden of the treachery that raised her
Rtas 'Vadum, Special Operations Commander as the games show him: a veteran Sangheili with a scarred half-blind face and one eye lost to the Flood, violet-silver harness, twin-bladed and unflinching
The Gravemind as the games imagine it: a vast mountain of Flood flesh under High Charity, a maw of tentacles and stacked corpses, speaking in the stolen voices of the dead, patient beyond all measure
Jarl Laila Law-Giver of Riften as the games show her: a grey-haired matron in Eastmarch furs, careworn and honorable, suspicious of the Black-Briars her hold can never quite touch
Jarl Igmund of Markarth as the games show him: a broad Reachman-reigning Nord noble in fur-lined holds-garb, silver-brown hair, caught between Silver-Blood coin and his father's debts
King Lysandus of Daggerfall as the games imagine him: a ghost-armored Breton king, chain and plate still rent by the wounds of Battlefield cry, loyal beyond death to a son and a warning
King Kurog gro-Bagrakh of Orsinium as the games show him: a powerfully built Orc king in forged plate, tusks capped in gold, a reformer's fire and an iron fist behind every promise

Warlord Gortwog gro-Nagorm of Orsinium as the games describe him: a canny aged Orc warlord in heavy mail, grey-green hide and yellowed tusks, fighting for his people's kingdom with law as well as steel

Fahara'jad the Forebearer King of Sentinel as the games imagine him: a Redguard monarch in Alik'r silks and a gold-embroidered turban, steel beneath ceremony, holding Hammerfell's coasts for crown and kin
High King Torygg of Skyrim as the games remember him: a young golden-haired Nord king in fine blue war-dress, earnest and boyish, dead in a duel that lit the province on fire

Count Janus Hassildor of Skingrad as the games show him: a pale imperious Cyrodilic noble with crimson eyes and immaculate velvet doublets, a reclusive vampire count ruling by fear and competence in equal parts

King Elhokar Kholin of Alethkar as the books show him: a young dark-haired Alethi king in regal blacks and gold, faintly unfinished stubble, painted-on glory seeking the moment he becomes worthy of it
Brightness Fen Tana of the Alethi court as the books show her: a poised Alethi noblewoman in a safe-hand gown of Havah silk, dark hair braided with gemstones, courtly steel and Thaylen wit

Shardbearer Eshonai, the Listener general as the books show her: a Parshendi warrior in carapace-warform armor with red-black marbled skin, greatsword at her back, a scholar's heart inside a soldier's form

Primarch Roboute Guilliman as the setting shows him: a god-high demigod in cobalt-blue Macragge plate edged with gold, the Aquila across his breast, stern patrician face of a living lawgiver awakened to a broken empire

Archmagos Belisarius Cawl as the setting shows him: an ancient Mechanicum archmagos of green robes and mechadendrites, half his skull replaced with chrome, a hoard of ten thousand years of heresy under his hood
Lord Castellan Ursarkar Creed as the setting shows him: a granite-jawed Cadian officer with grey stubble and a storm coat, chainsword at his hip, tanks on his mind and Cadia in his bones

Lord Commander Solar Macharius as the setting remembers him: a young fiery Imperial commander in gilded carapace, beardless and bright-eyed, the greatest conqueror since the Heresy, dying of faith and plague at the edge of the map

Saint Celestine the Living as the setting shows her: the Adepta Sororitas' returned saint in white-and-gold power armor, gauntleted hands spread with holy fire, wings of light at her back, serene beyond mortal fear

Ragnar Blackmane, Wolf Lord of the Space Wolves as the setting shows him: a young savage Fenrisian hero in grey-blue plate with wolf-pelt cloak, red beard, frost blade howling, the angriest of the Emperor's wolves
